concepts.mechanism_summary: Coppicing works by cutting a tree to a living stump (stool), which activates dormant buds on the stool. As the Wikipedia/search snippet states: 'A tree is cut back periodically to stimulate new growth through dormant buds on the living stump, or stool. These buds develop into sprouts, also called shoots, capable of growing firewood in approximately half the time it would take to grow the same amount of wood from seed.' The periodic harvest resets the cycle, allowing repeated biomass production from the same root system.

atoms.verbatim_quote: A tree is cut back periodically to stimulate new growth through dormant buds on the living stump, or stool
atoms.mechanism_atom: Cutting (decapitation) activates dormant buds on the stool, triggering resprouting

atoms.verbatim_quote: young tree stems are repeatedly cut down to near ground level, and the resulting living stumps are called stools. New growth emerges, and after a number of years, the coppiced trees are harvested, and the cycle begins anew
atoms.mechanism_atom: The harvest-regrowth cycle propagates iteratively from the same root stock, yielding biomass without replanting

atoms.verbatim_quote: Resprouting patterns are determined by axillary buds which either form new shoots or enter dormancy, with this decision essentially controlled by hormone signals including auxin, cytokinins, and strigolactones
atoms.mechanism_atom: Decapitation induces hormonal signaling (auxin, cytokinin, strigolactone balance) that governs bud fate decisions

concepts.mechanism_summary: Espalier works by pruning and physically tying woody plant branches to a rigid frame, constraining three-dimensional growth into a flat two-dimensional plane against a wall or trellis. The Wikipedia snippet states: 'controlling woody plant growth for the production of fruit, by pruning and tying branches to a frame. Plants are frequently shaped in formal patterns, flat against a structure such as a wall, fence, or trellis.' The wall reflects additional sunlight and retains heat, extending the growing season and enabling fruit production in marginal climates.

concepts.mechanism_summary: Nixtamalization treats maize in alkaline solution (typically limewater), dissolving hemicellulose that cements cell walls and loosening the hull (pericarp). The Wikipedia snippet states: 'The alkalinity helps the dissolution of hemicellulose, the major glue-like component of the maize cell walls, and loosens the hulls from the kernels.' This chemical transformation simultaneously frees bound niacin, reduces mycotoxins by up to 97-100%, increases calcium content, and improves grindability — a suite of nutritional and physical transformations triggered by a single pH change.

source_results.title: Retting | Fibre Separation Process for Hemp, Flax & Jute | Britannica
A Comprehensive Review on Bast Fibre Retting Process for Optimal Performance in Fibre-Reinforced Polymer Composites
Full article: Retting and Chemical Treatment of Natural Fibers – A Review

concepts.mechanism_summary: Retting separates bast fibers from non-fibrous stem tissue by selectively degrading the cementing matrix (primarily pectin and lignin) while leaving cellulose intact. The Wikipedia snippet states: 'The separation is primarily achieved through either a microbial or chemical action degradating the cementing compounds that bind the bast fibres to other plant tissues.' In water retting, anaerobic bacteria degrade pectin; in dew retting, aerobic fungi and bacteria on the field surface attack pectins and hemicellulose. The key insight is selective degradation: pectin-matrix destroyed, cellulose fibers preserved.

atoms.verbatim_quote: The separation is primarily achieved through either a microbial or chemical action degradating the cementing compounds that bind the bast fibres to other plant tissues, allowing the fibers to be isolated
atoms.mechanism_atom: Microbial or chemical degradation selectively separates target fibers from surrounding matrix by destroying the binding pectin/lignin cement while preserving cellulose

atoms.verbatim_quote: anaerobic bacteria degrade the cementing compounds, typically pectin, allowing the bast fibres to separate from the woody tissues, called shive, in the stem
atoms.mechanism_atom: Anaerobic microbial communities selectively degrade pectin cement, liberating aligned cellulose fiber bundles from the woody shive

atoms.verbatim_quote: Dew retting is a natural process wherein fibers are spread evenly in the field for 2–10 weeks after harvesting. Filamentous fungi or aerobic bacteria present in soil or plants attack non-cellulosic materials and remove pectins and hemicellulose without damaging cellulose
atoms.mechanism_atom: Dew retting transforms a composite stem into separated fibers through selective aerobic fungal/bacterial attack on non-cellulosic binders, leaving structural cellulose intact
